prompt: What does a host intrusion detection system watch?

choices.text: Every conversation crossing the segment it is plugged into
choices.why: That is the NIDS's view.

choices.text: One machine's files, processes, users and logs
choices.why: Right. It runs on the machine it watches.

choices.text: The firewall's rule counters
choices.why: Those belong to the firewall.

choices.text: Traffic between two other hosts on its segment
choices.why: It sees nothing on another machine.

prompt: Match each tool to the kind of sensor it is.
hint: The last row of the table.

pairs.right: a network sensor watching a segment
a host sensor recording what processes do

prompt: An intruder gains root on www. Which sensor's record of www's traffic can they not edit?

choices.text: The HIDS on www, because it is protected by its own agent
choices.why: Root on the host can tamper with the agent.

choices.text: Both, since each keeps a log
choices.why: A log on www is within reach of root on www.

choices.text: The NIDS on sensor
choices.why: Right. It runs on another machine.

choices.text: The access log of the proxy on www
choices.why: That file lives on the compromised host.

prompt: The stranger asked for /admin/ once over HTTP and once over HTTPS. How many alerts did the network sensor raise?
For the HTTPS request, what could the network sensor read?

choices.text: The path /admin/, but not the answer
choices.why: The path was encrypted.

choices.text: The client's address, port 443 and the name www.example.com
choices.why: Right. The name, and nothing about what was asked.

choices.text: The status code 200
choices.why: Only the proxy's log shows it.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: It recorded the TLS connection.

prompt: The rule for the admin path stays silent on HTTPS. Where does this lesson put detection of requests inside TLS?
hint: Who reads the request in the clear?

choices.text: In a second network sensor closer to www
choices.why: It sees the same ciphertext.

choices.text: In a stricter Suricata rule on the SNI
choices.why: The SNI names the site, not the path.

choices.text: In the firewall, by blocking port 443
choices.why: That would close the shop.

choices.text: Where TLS ends: the proxy's logs, a WAF there, or an agent on that host
choices.why: Right. That machine has the plaintext.

prompt: With most web traffic encrypted, what does a network sensor still see well? Choose all that apply.
hint: The last sentence of the section.

choices.text: Who talked to whom, and when
choices.why: Right. Addresses and times are outside the encryption.

choices.text: How much was sent, and in which protocol
choices.why: Right. Volumes and protocols stay visible.

choices.text: The paths requested inside HTTPS
choices.why: Encrypted, as the missing alert showed.

choices.text: The status code each HTTPS request got
choices.why: That came from the proxy's log.

prompt: With what exit code did aide --check end after the proxy's configuration was changed?
How many bytes larger did sites-enabled/shop become?
hint: Subtract the two sizes AIDE printed.

prompt: Why did AIDE report two changed entries for one edited file?

choices.text: It hashes each file twice, with two algorithms
choices.why: Watch names one hash, SHA-256.

choices.text: The directory's times moved too
choices.why: Right. The d line shows m and c changed.

choices.text: A TLS key under /etc/ssl/private changed at the same time
choices.why: Both entries are under /etc/nginx.

choices.text: The report counts the old and the new version
choices.why: It counts entries, and the directory is one.

prompt: AIDE's first run records how things are now, and that record, kept where an intruder cannot rewrite it, becomes the ___ for every later check.
hint: The word the section uses for it.

prompt: An intruder with root on www runs aide --init after editing the proxy's configuration. What does the next check report, and what would have prevented it?

choices.text: Exit code 4, because AIDE remembers the first database
choices.why: It compares against the file it is told to read.

choices.text: An error, since --init refuses a second run
choices.why: It builds a new database happily.

choices.text: No differences; a reference copied off the host
choices.why: Right. The rewritten database matches the edit.

choices.text: No differences; running the check more often
choices.why: More checks against a rewritten reference still agree.

prompt: Comparing www's listening sockets with the baseline showed what?

choices.text: Port 443 had stopped listening
choices.why: A removed line would start with <.

choices.text: A second nginx on port 80
choices.why: Port 80 was already in the baseline.

choices.text: socat listening on 0.0.0.0:8081
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: sshd listening on a new address, 192.0.2.80:22
choices.why: No port 22 appeared in either list.

prompt: Why did the network sensor see nothing of the new listener on 8081?
hint: What crosses the wire when a port opens?

choices.text: socat encrypts its traffic
choices.why: There was no traffic yet to encrypt.

choices.text: Suricata ignores ports above 1024
choices.why: It watches any port.

choices.text: The firewall of lesson 4 hid it from the DMZ
choices.why: The firewall is the only thing left in front of it, not a disguise.

choices.text: Nobody had connected to it yet
choices.why: Right. Opening a port puts nothing on the wire.

prompt: Match each host check to what a finding looks like.

pairs.right: a key in authorized_keys nobody issued
a shell spawned by the web server
a login at 3 a.m. from a new address

right_distractors: a TLS connection whose SNI is the shop

prompt: What does this lesson call putting the network's rows and the host's rows together?
hint: A SIEM does it for a company.

choices.text: Correlation
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: File integrity monitoring
choices.why: That is one of the host's checks.

choices.text: Deep packet inspection of both sensors' logs
choices.why: Packet inspection reads traffic, not logs.

choices.text: Baselining
choices.why: A baseline is what one check compares against.

prompt: For a camera on the office network, which sensor is the witness?

choices.text: A HIDS agent installed on the camera
choices.why: Cameras run no agent at all.

choices.text: The NIDS watching its segment
choices.why: Right. It sees what the camera sends.

choices.text: AIDE on the file server where the recordings land
choices.why: That watches the server's files, not the camera.

choices.text: The camera's own log, copied off daily
choices.why: An intruder in the camera controls that log.

prompt: www is compromised and the intruder edits its logs and AIDE reports. Which rows of the lesson's side-by-side table survive? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Alert 1000101 for /admin/ over HTTP
choices.why: Right. It is on sensor.

choices.text: The TLS connection to www.example.com
choices.why: Right. Also recorded on sensor.

choices.text: AIDE's report of 602 bytes becoming 744
choices.why: It sits on www, unless it was shipped off.

choices.text: The access log lines for both requests
choices.why: That log is on www.

prompt: Order the steps of setting up file integrity monitoring on a new server.
hint: A reference comes before any comparison.
items: name the directories that matter in the configuration
copy the reference where the server cannot rewrite it
run aide --check on a schedule and send the report
trap: A check run before the reference exists has nothing to compare against.

prompt: A nightly AIDE report shows /etc/ssh/sshd_config changed. No change request mentions it, and the listening ports match the baseline. What is the reading?
hint: Two checks answer two different questions.

choices.text: Nothing to investigate, since no new port opened
choices.why: A changed SSH setting opens no port.

choices.text: A false positive, because the ports check is newer
choices.why: The two checks do not overrule each other.

choices.text: It is the report to read first
choices.why: Right. A change with no change request.

choices.text: Proof of intrusion, so the server is rebuilt at once
choices.why: AIDE says it changed, not who changed it or why.

prompt: The NIDS logs a new outbound connection from the database server at 02:10, and the database server's HIDS reports a new process at 02:10. Why is this worth more than either alone?

choices.text: The NIDS confirms the HIDS agent is running
choices.why: It saw traffic, not the agent.

choices.text: Two alerts double the severity score
choices.why: The point is agreement, not a sum.

choices.text: The HIDS can now read the encrypted connection
choices.why: Correlation does not decrypt anything.

choices.text: Two weak signals, same time and machine, make a strong one from independent sources
choices.why: Right. That is correlation.
